sentences.text: Cacibupteryx was a rhamphorhynchid pterosaur found in the Upper Jurassic Jagua Formation of Pinar del Río, Cuba.
Researchers described it as a relatively large form, though they did not estimate its wingspan or total length.
The genus name combines the Taíno word Cacibu, meaning "Lord of the Sky", with the Greek word pteryx, meaning "wing".
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — includes a partial skull missing the snout tip, teeth, and lower jaws, plus fragmentary left wing bones.
The genus was named in 2004 by Zulma Gasparini, Marta Fernández, and Marcelo de la Fuente.
The type species of the genus is Cacibupteryx caribensis.
Phylogenetic analyses place Cacibupteryx in the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae, closely related to Rhamphorhynchus and Nesodactylus.
Cacibupteryx lived from the Oxfordian to the Tithonian stages, between 161.5 and 143.1 million years ago.
While recent revisions support Cacibupteryx as a basal rhamphorhynchid, researcher David Unwin suggests it may belong to the subfamily Scaphognathinae, known for robust jaws.
